problems.title: Inverse of a restricted square-root function
problems.question: Find the inverse of y=√(x−2), x≥4.
problems.idea: Use the governing formula and check signs, domains and possible configurations.
formulas: Swap input and output and solve for the new output.
steps: The original range is [√2,∞). Squaring gives x=y²+2, so the inverse is y=x²+2 with input x≥√2.

problems.title: Quarter-power substitutions cancel a long product
problems.question: Simplify $\frac{x-y}{x^{3/4}-x^{1/2}y^{1/4}}\frac{x^{1/2}y^{1/4}+x^{1/4}y^{1/2}}{x^{1/2}+y^{1/2}}\frac{x^{1/2}y^{-1/4}}{x^{1/2}+2x^{1/4}y^{1/4}+y^{1/2}}$; evaluate at x=16,y=1/4.
problems.idea: Use the governing formula and check signs, domains and possible configurations.
formulas: Put u=x¹/⁴,v=y¹/⁴, with x,y>0 and x≠y.
steps: The factors become $(u+v)(u^2+v^2)/u^2$, $uv(u+v)/(u^2+v^2)$, and $u^2/[v(u+v)^2]$.
All common factors cancel, leaving u=x¹/⁴. At x=16 the value is 2.

problems.title: Nested roots and their domain
problems.question: Simplify $\sqrt[4]{a^5\sqrt[3]{a^4}}\,\sqrt[4]{a^2\sqrt[3]{a^{-1}}}$.
problems.idea: Use the governing formula and check signs, domains and possible configurations.
formulas: The inverse excludes zero and the fourth roots require a>0; then powers may be combined.
steps: The exponents of a are (5+4/3)/4=19/12 and (2−1/3)/4=5/12.
Their sum is 2, giving a².

problems.title: Two equations using roots as new variables
problems.question: Solve (a) $(5x+1)^{1/3}+(5x+1)^{1/6}=6$; (b) $\sqrt{x+2\sqrt{x-1}}+\sqrt{x-2\sqrt{x-1}}=2$.
problems.idea: Use the governing formula and check signs, domains and possible configurations.
formulas: (a) Set t=(5x+1)¹/⁶≥0. (b) Set u=√(x−1)≥0 and use √(v²)=|v|.
steps: (a) t²+t−6=(t−2)(t+3)=0 gives t=2. Thus 5x+1=64 and x=63/5.
(b) x=u²+1 makes the radical sum |u+1|+|u−1|. It is 2 exactly for 0≤u≤1.
Hence the second solution is 1≤x≤2.

problems.title: A radical undefined for every real input
problems.question: For which a is √(−x²+2(a−1)x−a+1) undefined for every real x?
problems.idea: Use the governing formula and check signs, domains and possible configurations.
steps: To have no nonnegative radicand at all, its maximum must be strictly negative. Thus (a−1)(a−2)<0.
This holds for 1<a<2. At either endpoint a zero radicand would be defined, so endpoints are excluded.

problems.title: Two graphs and a complete solution-count classification
problems.question: (a) Graph y=floor(√x). (b) Graph y=(3−|x|)/(|x|−1), and count its intersections with y=a.
problems.idea: Use the governing formula and check signs, domains and possible configurations.
steps: (a) Draw horizontal steps: y=0 on [0,1), y=1 on [1,4), y=2 on [4,9), etc. The left endpoint is filled and right endpoint open.
(b) The graph is even, with vertical asymptotes x=±1 and horizontal asymptote y=−1. For 0≤t<1 it decreases from −3 to −∞; for t>1 it decreases from +∞ toward −1.
Every positive t corresponds to two inputs ±t; t=0 corresponds to one. Therefore a<−3 gives two roots, a=−3 one root, −3<a≤−1 none, and a>−1 two.

problems.title: An equilateral triangle inside a regular pentagon
problems.question: M lies inside regular pentagon ABCDE and DEM is equilateral. Find AMC.
problems.idea: Use the governing formula and check signs, domains and possible configurations.
formulas: Pentagon interior angles are 108°; equal sides form isosceles triangles.
steps: At E, AEM=108−60=48°. Since EA=EM, triangle AEM has base angles EMA=EAM=66°.
By symmetry triangle CDM gives DMC=66°. Around M, the other consecutive angles are 66°,60°,66°.
The remaining angle AMC is 360−66−60−66=168°.

problems.title: Regular polygon side count from adjacent contact radii
problems.question: Radii to incircle contact points on adjacent sides of a regular n-gon make 20°. Find n.
problems.idea: Use the governing formula and check signs, domains and possible configurations.
formulas: The equal contact-radius angles partition the full 360° turn.
steps: 360/n=20, giving n=18.

problems.title: Four equal circular lenses in a square
problems.question: In the source figure, inward semicircles are drawn on the four sides of a square of side a. Find the total shaded lens area.
problems.idea: Use the governing formula and check signs, domains and possible configurations.
formulas: Each lens comprises two 90° sectors of radius a/2 minus two right isosceles triangles.
steps: There are four disjoint lens interiors. Their total is a²(π−2)/2.

problems.title: Hexagon area divided by incircle area
problems.question: Find regular-hexagon area divided by the area of its incircle.
problems.idea: Use the governing formula and check signs, domains and possible configurations.
formulas: For side s, hexagon area=3√3s²/2 and inradius=√3s/2.
steps: The circle area is 3πs²/4. Dividing gives (3√3/2)/(3π/4)=2√3/π.
